Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Nova Consumer Goods third quarter Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing up questions will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Nova Consumer Goods' third quarter results. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; and other members of our leadership team, including Taylor Kim, our Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Nova Consumer Goods delivered a solid third quarter, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover four key areas. First, our overall financial performance, highlighted by robust organic sales growth. Second, brand performance and innovation, tied to our key strategic priorities and progress. Third, supply chain and operational efficiency, including the decomposition of that organic growth into volume, price, and mix. And fourth, our outlook for the remainder of the year, informed by our promotional strategy and effectiveness.

Let me start with a high-level view. We're seeing balanced growth across our portfolio, with strength in health and wellness and emerging markets helping offset softer areas. Our Accelerate 2025 playbook is delivering, as evidenced by market share gains and e-commerce acceleration. We've made tangible progress on premiumization, sustainability, digital initiatives, and supply chain resilience, positioning us ahead of peers in this elevation economy.

I will now turn the call over to Jordan to provide more detail on our financial results.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $3.45 billion, representing a 6.2% increase compared to the prior year. Gross margin was 48.2%, driven by pricing discipline, mix shift, and productivity gains that more than offset commodity inflation. Operating income was $685 million, up 12% year-over-year. Diluted earnings per share were $1.28, exceeding our guidance midpoint.

Turning to the headline metric that best reflects the health of our core business: organic sales growth, which excludes the impacts of acquisitions, divestitures, and foreign exchange translation—giving you a clean view of our underlying performance driven by volume, pricing, and mix. I'm pleased to report that Q3 organic sales grew 5.8% year-over-year, accelerating from 4.2% in Q2 and marking our sixth straight quarter of positive growth. This came in ahead of our guidance midpoint and outperformed the CPG industry average. Breaking it down at the total company level, volume contributed 1.9%, pricing added 2.4%, and mix contributed 1.5%, reflecting disciplined execution amid moderating inflation pressures across our key markets.

Let me drill into the segments, where we saw balanced contributions. Our powerhouse Health & Wellness division—think our flagship NovaVital protein bars and PureEssence functional beverages—delivered 6.8% organic growth, fueled by 3.2% volume gains from strong repeat purchases and market share expansion. IRI data shows us gaining 110 basis points in household penetration in U.S. grocery channels, now at 28.5% ACV. Premiumization played a big role here, with mix up 3.6% as consumers traded up to our zero-sugar and plant-based SKUs, mirroring trends we've seen at peers like Kellogg's and Mondelez.

In Household Essentials, organic growth was solid at 3.9%, driven by pricing actions to offset raw material costs—laundry pods and multi-surface cleaners saw mid-single-digit price realization. Volume held steady at +0.7%, supported by our 'EcoShield' sustainable packaging launch, which boosted distribution by 15% in big-box retailers like Walmart and Target.

Our Beauty & Personal Care segment grew 2.4% organically, a slight deceleration from Q2 due to softer demand in mass-premium shampoos amid economic headwinds. However, innovation mitigated this: our new AI-personalized skincare line, powered by our proprietary 'SkinGenius' app, drove 12% trial rates in e-commerce, helping us claw back 40 bps of NMV share per Circana scans.

Regionally, performance was robust but varied. North America, 55% of our sales, led with 5.6% organic growth—volume up 2.8% on the back of velocity gains in club channels like Costco, where our bulk snack packs outperformed by 200 bps versus the category. Pricing/mix of 2.8% benefited from targeted elasticity testing, keeping us ahead of P&G's reported pricing in the region.

EMEA faced headwinds from persistent inflation and energy costs, delivering 1.8% organic growth. Volumes were flat as consumers in the UK and Germany stretched budgets, but we gained share in discount channels like Aldi through our value-pack relaunch. Pricing contributed 1.8%, moderated from Q2 to preserve affordability.

Asia-Pacific was a bright spot at 6.1%, with India and China driving the bus: volumes up 4.2% on sachet innovations tailored for emerging middle-class consumers, akin to Unilever's strategies there. We expanded into 5,000 new kirana stores in India, lifting rural penetration by 8%.

Latin America rounded out at 2.9%, resilient despite FX volatility, with Brazil's beverage refreshers growing 7% on summer promotions and Mexico holding firm via in-store sampling.

This growth underscores our strategic playbook. We've invested $250 million in supply chain resilience—including a new aseptic filling line in Texas that cut lead times 25%—enabling faster shelf replenishment and supporting +1.2% velocity improvement across the portfolio. E-commerce now represents 18% of sales, up from 12% last year, with Amazon velocity 30% above brick-and-mortar averages, driven by Subscribe & Save penetration hitting 22%.

On trends, we're capitalizing on health & indulgence convergence, like our low-cal indulgence snacks; sustainability, with 80% of new products recyclable by 2024; and personalization via data analytics from our loyalty app, now with 15 million active users. Market share is up 60 bps YTD per NIQ, outpacing peers like Colgate-Palmolive and Reckitt.

Now, let's unpack that organic sales growth decomposition in more detail, which came in at a robust 5.8% for the quarter—well ahead of our guided range and accelerating from Q2. This marks our sixth straight quarter of positive organic growth amid a still-challenging macroeconomic backdrop, including persistent inflation in key input costs like cocoa, palm oil, and energy, which have risen 12-15% year-over-year globally.

For those new to our framework, we decompose it into volume, price, and mix. This granularity helps illustrate not just top-line momentum, but the health and sustainability of that growth.

At the total company level: volume +1.9%—driven by share gains across 70% of our portfolio, with particular strength in high-velocity SKUs. Units per store increased 1.2 points, reflecting improved shelf velocity and distribution expansion—we added 15,000 points of distribution globally, including 8,000 in e-commerce channels. Premium volume was especially resilient, up 4.1%, fueled by innovations like our NovaPure plant-based snacks line, which saw 25% unit growth in North America.

Price: +2.4%—disciplined pricing actions offset 60% of our input cost inflation, with list prices up modestly but effectively managed through everyday low pricing in mass channels and targeted promotional resets. We avoided aggressive hikes that could cede share.

Mix: +1.5%—premiumization continues to be a tailwind, with consumers trading up to our 'Nova Elite' tier across categories. This shift represented 2.3 points of benefit from higher-margin products like organic beauty regimens and functional beverages, partially offset by 0.8 points of drag from value-pack promotions in emerging markets.

This split underscores balanced growth—no single lever dominating—which positions us well for margin expansion.

Segment breakdown: Beauty & Personal Care, 28% of sales, +7.2% organic—volume +3.1%, price +2.8%, mix +1.3%. Market share up 80 bps per Nielsen; NovaGlow serums gained 30% volume via TikTok-driven virality and prestige door expansions at Sephora.

Health & Wellness, 22% of sales, +4.9%—volume +1.2%, price +2.7%, mix +1.0%. Functional nutrition like VitaBoost probiotics up 18% on immunity trends; pricing captured 70% of whey protein cost inflation.

Snacks & Beverages, 35% of sales, +5.1%—volume +2.4%, price +1.9%, mix +0.8%. Volume led by salty snacks like NovaCrunch; e-comm mix up 15%.

Household Essentials, 15% of sales, +3.7%—volume +0.3%, price +2.5%, mix +0.9%. Softer volume due to pantry destocking, but share stable.

Geographically: North America, 45% of sales, +6.4%—volume +2.8%, price +2.1%, mix +1.5%. Europe +4.2%—volume +1.1%, price +2.6%, mix +0.5%. Emerging Markets +6.9%—volume +2.5%, price +2.8%, mix +1.6%. Rest of World +3.8%.

This reflects our Growth Accelerator playbook: AI-powered pricing across 80% of SKUs, SKU rationalization pruning 1,200 low-velocity items, 40% of growth from new products with sustainability claims, omnichannel push lifting e-comm velocity.

Turning to our key strategic priorities and progress year-to-date. Our strategy remains laser-focused on delivering sustainable, profitable growth in a dynamic CPG landscape marked by persistent inflation, shifting consumer behaviors, and heightened competition from both national brands and private labels. We've structured our priorities around four pillars: portfolio premiumization and innovation, sustainability and ESG leadership, digital acceleration and consumer-centricity, and supply chain resilience and productivity.

First, portfolio premiumization and innovation. We're doubling down on high-margin, high-growth categories like health & wellness, plant-based alternatives, and functional snacks—segments growing at 8-10% CAGR per Nielsen and IRI data. Our core power brands, including NovaVital protein bars and PureEssence clean-label beverages, now represent 65% of our portfolio, up from 58% last year. This shift drove organic sales growth of 6.2% in Q3, with premium SKUs contributing 75% of that upside.

Progress includes the launch of our NovaVital GLP-Ready line—low-calorie, high-protein snacks tailored to the GLP-1 medication boom, which could shrink the snacking market. Early results: 15% household penetration within eight weeks, capturing 2.1 points of market share. In North America, premiumization lifted ASPs by 4.8% YoY. Internationally, NovaVital grew 12% in Asia-Pacific via e-commerce partnerships.

We'll invest $250M over FY24 in R&D for 20 new premium innovations, targeting 70% premium portfolio mix by 2025.

Second, sustainability and ESG leadership. Euromonitor reports 62% of shoppers prioritize sustainable packaging, and we're 45% to our 100% recyclable goal by 2030. In Q3, we converted 80% of NovaFresh household care bottles to 100% rPET, reducing virgin plastic by 25,000 tons annually, yielding $45M in savings and boosting brand favorability by 18 points. In Europe, sustainable SKUs grew 14% YoY. Emerging markets like Latin America cut Scope 3 emissions by 12%. FY24 capex includes $150M for circular economy tech.

Third, digital acceleration and consumer-centricity. E-commerce is 22% of sales, up from 15% in 2022. Our NovaNow app hit 5M active users, generating $180M TTM sales—35% YoY—with 40% repeat rates. AI personalization increased basket sizes 22%. Digital velocity added share in North America and Asia.

We'll deploy $100M for omnichannel AI, aiming for 30% digital mix by 2026.

Finally, supply chain resilience and productivity. Our Agile Supply 2.0 program delivered $320M in gross savings YTD through precision farming, vendor consolidation, and GenAI forecasting. Inventory days down 18% to 45 days. Hedging covers 70% of cocoa and palm oil. Productivity rose across regions, boosting EBITDA margins to 19.8%, +120bps YoY.

These priorities are delivering: 5.8% organic growth YTD, 150bps market share expansion, 2.5x net debt to EBITDA.

Now, on our promotional strategy and effectiveness—a critical lever where trade spend is 20-25% of gross revenue. In Q3, total promotional spend was $285 million, up 8% YoY, or 22% of net revenue. Despite the uptick, we achieved 3.2x ROI, up 15% from last year, through right-sizing promotions amid stretched elasticities.

This delivered 18% sales lift during events, with equivalized base volume growing 4%, outpacing category averages. Core power brands like Zest beverages and PureClean detergents got 60% of spend, generating 22% lift. Innovation SKUs like NutriCrunch saw 25% trial and 4.1x ROI.

Our PromoOptix dashboard integrates POS and shopper data, reducing cannibalization to 8%.

Tech like AI Price Optimization Engine improved forecast accuracy to 92%. Digital promos are 35% of budget, with 2.5x higher conversion on personalized offers.

Regionally: North America 3.5x ROI; Europe 2.8x; Emerging Markets 4.2x, with strong results in Mexico and India.

Learnings: quality over quantity, cutting low-ROI promos 25%; shopper-centric funding; sustainability integration. Q4 promo intensity flat, targeting 3.5x ROI.

Looking forward, we expect Q4 organic growth of 4-6%, with volume inflecting on holidays. Risks around commodities, but hedging covers 70% through FY25. We're positioned for mid-teens EPS growth.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for submitting questions will be provided. Our first question comes from Mike Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Chen:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your consumer spending habits?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Mike. Inflation continues to pressure consumer budgets, particularly in mass channels where elasticity has stretched to 1.5-2.0 in snacks and household. That said, our balanced decomposition—volume resilience from premium innovations and pricing discipline offsetting 60% of input costs—shows we're navigating it well. Premiumization is key; consumers are trading up selectively in health and wellness, as seen in our 4.1% premium volume growth. We're ahead of peers by maintaining velocity through targeted EDLP and avoiding aggressive hikes. Regionally, North America and emerging markets are holding firm, while EMEA volumes are flat but share-positive in discounts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Patel with JPMorgan.

Lisa Patel:
Regarding your new product NovaVital GLP-Ready, what are the projections for its market impact?

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Lisa. NovaVital GLP-Ready is off to a strong start, hitting 15% household penetration in eight weeks and capturing 2.1 share points in functional nutrition per IRI. Tailored for the GLP-1 boom, we're projecting $150 million in FY24 sales, scaling to $400 million by 2026 as the medication market expands. Market impact includes 5-7% category uplift via health-indulgence convergence, with e-comm driving 30% of initial volume. We'll support with $50 million in marketing, targeting 25% repeat rates and expansion into Europe and Asia next year.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Ruiz with Morgan Stanley.

David Ruiz:
Can you provide more details on the promotional spending for the quarter?

Jordan Lee:
Sure, David. As I detailed earlier, Q3 promo spend was $285 million, 22% of net revenue, delivering 3.2x ROI—up 15% YoY. We focused on high-elasticity events, achieving 18% lift overall, with core brands at 22% and innovations at 25% trial. AI optimization and digital personalization boosted efficiency, reducing cannibalization and lifting conversions 2.5x. Emerging markets shone at 4.2x ROI. For Q4, intensity holds flat, targeting 3.5x amid holidays, supporting our 4-6% organic guide.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your questions and participation in today's call. We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders, powered by our strategic priorities, balanced growth drivers, and optimized promotions. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Nova Consumer Goods third quarter Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
